answer.evidence: radon/metrics.py:150 defines mi_rank(score), which maps a maintainability index to a letter with `chr(65 + (9 - score >= 0) + (19 - score >= 0))`. A is score > 19, B is 9 < score <= 19, and C is score <= 9. So 9 gives C and 19 gives B, and both thresholds are inclusive on the lower grade. mi_visit and mi_compute in the same file produce the score. I did not open radon/raw.py, radon/complexity.py or radon/visitors.py, and I did not read the handoff_refs files. The A, B and D minute allocations are estimates, not findings. complexity.py has its own letter ranking, so B gets some time to confirm it is separate from the MI ranking.
